warrant: The graded histories and frames follow the Vlasov-Poisson sheath path: non-periodic Poisson boundary conditions, absorbing and reflecting species boundaries and the LTE projection of two species. In `rt_vp_sheath_1x1v_p2.c`, `n0` (line 74) is the reference density that sets both initial Maxwellians and, through the Debye length, the domain; the two-ULP variant therefore moves every graded value at the level of the arithmetic, while a wrong Poisson boundary condition, a wrong wall flux or a wrong charge sign changes them at order one. The bound atol=1e-10, rtol=1e-10 was set on 2026-09-06 from the calibration selfcheck on the x86 worker 136.114.2.6 (1 cpu, 4 GB, Docker): the two-ULP variant used at most 9.0e-3 of it and the strict-IEEE altbuild at most 6.8e-3 (worst files `elc-imom.gkyl` and `field-energy.gkyl`), a headroom of about 112x over the larger legitimate perturbation, while the faults named above move the graded values at order one. Component overrides: `elc-imom.gkyl` (3 values per sample) component 1 atol=1e+11, rtol=1e-10; `ion-imom.gkyl` (3 values per sample) component 1 atol=1e+07, rtol=1e-10. Those components are cancellation residuals or near-zero moments (here the parallel momenta of a sheath whose net flow starts at zero): their absolute spread under the two legitimate perturbations sits far above the file-level bound while their scale is orders of magnitude below the other components of the same history, so each keeps its own decade-rounded bound at the same 100x rule and stays fully graded.
